statement.p: Find the first four terms of the Taylor series for the function \displaystyle \frac{5}{x} about the point a = 2. (Your answers should include the variable x when appropriate.)

static.solution:
\displaystyle \frac{5}{x} and its first three derivatives are
f(x) = \displaystyle \frac{5}{x}, f'(x) = -{5\over x^2}, f''(x) = {10\over x^3}, and f'''(x) = -{30\over x^4}. Thus, evaluating these at x = 2, we get the terms
term 0 = {{5\over2}}
term 1 = -{{5\over4}}(x - 2)
term 2 = {{5\over8}}(x - 2)^2, and
term 3 = -{{5\over16}}(x - 2)^3.
Thus the series is \displaystyle \frac{5}{x} = {{5\over2}} - {{5\over4}}(x - 2) + {{5\over8}}(x - 2)^2 - {{5\over16}}(x - 2)^3 + \cdots.
